**Where we stand.** No strategy is net positive after costs. tsmom has the only gross edge (+0.06 R, t 2.4–2.6),
and it is negative net (−0.014 R at 4h before swap). Meta-models add nothing (AUC ≈ 0.50). The Q4 trial budget is
spent (20/20); trials resume 2027-01-01. So the ranking favours two things: work that can still flip tsmom or find a
new edge cheaply (**FIND**), and work that must exist before the system runs unattended on demo (**RUN**). Every
expected-impact figure below is uncertain. None of these items is expected to create profit on its own.

Rank = expected impact on net profit and safety ÷ effort. Size: S < 1 day, M 1–3 days, L > 3 days.
Status: ready / in progress / in review / done / rejected. Item numbers are stable ids; the order of the table is
the rank.

Value: momentum edges are made in the exits. Labels cannot test exits the engine cannot run, and exits are never

### 8. Stop rule and gate thresholds in code
Value: governance the design commits to before the first paper trade, and the safe-direction automatic halt (RUN).
Acceptance:
- A daily job computes P6 (after 18 months, more than 500 pooled trades and a lower 90% bound on expectancy below
  zero, or any single loss larger than the weekly cap). A breach sets the existing system halt. Only the owner clears
  it. Tested on synthetic trade sets on each side of each condition.
- P7: the trade-count and time thresholds for each phase gate live in `settings.yaml`. A job writes `met / not met`
  with the evidence to `state/phase_state.json`. It never flips the phase itself. Tested.
- The dashboard shows the stop-rule and gate status (API schema regenerated).

Depends on: the owner signs off the threshold values. Rows: P6, P7.

Status (2026-10-10): done in `goldbot/ops/gates_phase.py`, `run.py gates` / `gate-evidence`, health checks

acceptance above, as briefed for this change: a stop-rule breach is a health FAIL and a Telegram alert that

    GBP account at GBPUSD 1.33: £1,000, 15m stop $10.90 → realised 0.82%; a USD account gives decisions identical

    mixed currencies, failing closed (A8).

    change. Reviews: trading-safety, code, ui-ux (card label).

  lines still run 00:00-24:00 UTC (`goldbot/telegram/digest.py` `build_digest`). Its month line and the monthly and
  performance reports use the opportunity day (`goldbot/ops/report_days.py`). So a close at 23:00 UTC is in
  yesterday's trades line and in today's month line. Acceptance:
  - for a digest built on day D, "Yesterday" covers [D-2 22:00, D-1 22:00) UTC, the opportunity day D-1, through
    `report_days` (no new day arithmetic in the digest);
  - the header reads "Yesterday (to 22:00 UTC)" with the weekday and date of D-1;
  - tests at 21:59 and 22:00 UTC, on a Monday digest (the Sunday reopen counts on Monday), and in a US DST week;
  - the risk lines (loss-cap use) stay on the risk day, 00:00 UTC; no limit changes;
  - reviews: code, ui-ux (Telegram wording).
  Sweep 2026-10-16 (product owner): accountable `implementer`, due 2026-10-19. Acceptance as above.
- **57. risk_day_anchor is read by no code: pin it or make it real.** Value: `config/settings.yaml` says
  `risk_day_anchor: { tz: UTC, time: "00:00" }  # loss caps reset`, and `Settings.risk_day_anchor` loads it, but no
  code reads it. The 00:00 UTC risk day is decided separately in five places: `timeutil.risk_day` (gate `new_day`,
  `throttle.entries_on_day`, perf_report's drawdown), the runner's UTC `.date()` shortcut in `_roll_risk_period`,
  `entry_status._next_day`, `gate._risk_week`, and the supervisor through the engines' `day_start_equity`. An owner
  who sets it in `settings.local.yaml` believes the caps' reset has moved; it has not (HANDOFF 2026-10-16, "Finding:
  risk_day_anchor"). Acceptance:
  - a Settings validator refuses any `risk_day_anchor` other than UTC 00:00 at load, naming the fixed risk day; the
    same for `feature_day_anchor` other than America/New_York 13:30, or the setting is wired to `resample`;
  - a test proves an edited anchor fails to load, and the shipped yaml loads;
  - no change to when any cap resets (a test pins `new_day` at 00:00 UTC); rollback-safe (an older release ignores
    the key);
  - moving the risk day itself (for example to the 22:00 UTC roll) is a separate owner decision. It needs one
    shared risk-day function for all five places, a migration for the persisted reset time, and a trading-safety
    review;
  - **before the validator ships** (trading-safety review of the north-star day lane, 2026-10-16): check each
    server's `config/settings.local.yaml` for `risk_day_anchor` and `feature_day_anchor`, because a server that sets
    either would stop loading its settings after the deploy. Put the validator's exact error text and the fix
    (delete the key) into `docs/RUNBOOK.md` in the same change.
  Sweep 2026-10-16 (product owner): accountable `implementer`, due 2026-10-19; trading-safety review. The server `settings.local.yaml` check (last bullet) is done by sre on the boxes before the validator ships. Acceptance as above.
- **58. Fail closed on heartbeats stamped in the future (found 2026-10-16).** Value: every liveness check had the
  shape `now - ts > limit`. A `ts` in the future (a clock step, a bad write, a state backup restored from a box whose
  clock ran fast) made the age negative, and a NaN made every comparison False, so the heartbeat read as fresh for
  ever. A dead supervisor would then never halt the engines. Two tests in tests/test_telegram_status.py relied on
  this until 14 Oct. Acceptance:
  - `Supervisor.engine_should_halt` halts with `supervisor_heartbeat_future` when `supervisor.json` is stamped more
    than `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S` (5 s) ahead, and with `supervisor_state_unreadable` when `ts` is not a finite
    number or the file is not an object; a skew of 1-2 s does not halt;
  - the supervisor halts every entry (`engine_heartbeat_future`, file named in `future_engines`) on an engine file
    stamped more than 5 s ahead;
  - both reasons have plain-language text on the dashboard and Telegram (entry_status `REASONS`) and a RUNBOOK row;
  - health fails `supervisor`, `engine:<account>`, `engine_loop:<account>`, `heartbeat:<service>` and `scheduler`
    (warns `alerts`) on a stamp more than `HEALTH_CLOCK_AHEAD_S` (5 s) ahead of max(the pass's `now`, the wall
    clock), so a slow pass never flags a stamp written while it ran, and on a NaN or non-numeric stamp;
  - the Feeds page shows such a supervisor heartbeat as not reporting, the dashboard does not show combined caps from
    it, and a bridge verdict confirmed in the future counts as `unchecked`;
  - tests/test_heartbeat_clock_ahead.py covers each: beyond tolerance fails, within tolerance does not, NaN/str fails.
- **59. Engine state keeps moving on the host clock while the market is closed.** Value: with the market closed
  (weekend, weekday daily break 20:59-22:02 UTC) the terminal repeats its last quote, so the tick stamp is frozen and
  the tick-time state cadence (`state_every_s`) never fired. `engine_<acct>.json` went stale, and health compared its
  `bridge_compat.checked_at` with the wall clock: FAIL after 5 min, a Healthchecks.io `/fail` every 2 min all
  weekend, and a FAIL/recovered pair every weekday evening, which masks a real outage. Acceptance:
  - on the live clock, and only while the session table has the market closed, the state file is rewritten every
    `state_every_s` of host time when no write happened (any write restarts it; a host clock stepped back rewrites
    it in any session; an unreadable session table never does), so `bridge_compat:<acct>` and `engine:<acct>` stay OK through a frozen-tick weekend and the
    daily break (`tests/test_closed_market_state_cadence.py`);
  - the age rules are not skipped: an engine that writes nothing still FAILs `bridge_compat` on the weekend and
    `engine` after the reopen, and a feed frozen in an OPEN session still FAILs `bridge_compat` after 5 min and
    `engine` after 45 min (review HIGH);
  - the dashboard's entry status shows only "Market closed", not "stale data", when the engine says the market is
    closed;
  - the host-clock write only republishes: no account read, no stage machine, kill switch, weekend rule or other
    exit step, and no EngineState field changes; `last_tick_age_s`, `tick_ahead_s` and `market_closed` in the file
    are restated on the host clock so they stay true;
  - the write rate stays one per `state_every_s`, with today's fsync rules; replays (tick clock) are unchanged.
- **60. Approval window expiry trusts a future-stamped proposal (review of BACKLOG 58, 2026-10-16).** Value:
  `Proposal.expired` (goldbot/telegram/approvals.py:120) is `time.time() > created + window_s`, the same
  `now - ts > limit` shape BACKLOG 58 closed for heartbeats. A backward clock step of S seconds stretches the owner's
  90 s window by S, and a pending file stamped in the future (a restored backup, a bad write) stays approvable for
  longer than 90 s. The RiskGate runs again at approval, so the caps still hold, but the `EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED`
  contract (an entry the owner did not confirm within 90 s never opens) loosens. Accountable: trading-safety-reviewer;
  built by the implementer; due 2026-10-23. Acceptance:
  - a proposal whose `created` is more than `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S` (5 s) ahead of now counts as expired, never
    approvable (`goldbot.data.timeutil.heartbeat_problem` or the same rule), and a non-finite `created` too;
  - the engine also holds a monotonic deadline per proposal it raised (`time.monotonic()` at creation + `window_s`),
    and refuses an approval after it whatever the wall clock says; a restart drops the deadline and the proposal
    (fail closed);
  - the bus, Telegram and dashboard show such a proposal as expired, and the digest counts it as `EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED`;
  - tests: `created` 10 s ahead is expired; 2 s ahead is still open; a backward wall-clock step during the window does
    not let an approval through after the monotonic deadline; NaN or a string `created` is expired.
